risks.risk: Engine identity (make/engine code) is not readable, so the exact match to your car is uncertain.
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the engine code/label (usually on the engine block or transmission bell housing) plus the VIN plate or the exact donor car details.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic complete engine assembly with unknown engine code (worst-case fitment risk).

risks.risk: Unknown working condition (could be damaged, incomplete, or seized). Photos don’t show compression test, oil condition, or whether it turns freely.
risks.proof: Video of the engine cranking/turning by hand or starter (if possible), plus a short test result (compression/leakdown) or proof it was running before removal.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not proven working (worst case: treat as not working / needs overhaul).

risks.risk: Completeness: photos may not include all required parts (ECU, wiring harness, sensors, starter/alternator, turbo/ancillaries depending on engine).
risks.proof: A full inventory photo/clip laid out: ECU, harness, starter, alternator, sensors, intake/exhaust manifolds, turbo (if applicable), and all brackets/bolts.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially incomplete (worst case: missing some ancillaries).

risks.risk: Damage during removal/transport (bent mounts, cracked housings, broken connectors) can’t be confirmed from these angles.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all mounting points, oil pan area, timing cover area, and any cracked/broken connectors.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as may have removal/transport damage (worst case: repair needed).

proof_requests: Clear close-up of the engine code/label on the block/bell housing (and any part number stickers).
Video showing the engine turning freely (crank by hand or starter) and/or proof it was running before removal.
Confirm completeness: list what is included (ECU, harness, starter, alternator, sensors, turbo/supercharger if any) with photos of each item.
Close-ups of mounting points and any visible cracks/damage areas.
response.reason: The photos show a complete engine assembly, but the exact engine identity and working/completeness condition are not verifiable from the images provided, so a reliable worst-case price cannot be matched to the comparables.
